Bregman centroids and dispersions of a reliability profile

Source: R/algebra-related.R
bregman_centroid.Rd

bregman_centroid() computes the centroid of the site reliabilities under one of three Bregman divergences, on either side of the divergence, and bregman_dispersion() the average divergence at that centroid.

Usage

bregman_centroid(
  S,
  potential = c("kl", "squared", "burg"),
  side = c("first", "second")
)

bregman_dispersion(
  S,
  potential = c("kl", "squared", "burg"),
  side = c("first", "second")
)

Arguments

S

Site reliabilities, a numeric vector of numbers strictly between 0 and 1, as returned by site_reliability().

potential

The convex function that defines the divergence: one of "kl" (the default), "squared" or "burg". See Details.

side

Which argument of the divergence the centroid takes: "first" (the default) or "second".

Value

A number: the centroid, between 0 and 1, or the dispersion, of at least 0.

Details

A strictly convex function \(\phi\) defines the divergence \(D_\phi(x, y) = \phi(x) - \phi(y) - \phi'(y)(x - y)\). The first-argument centroid minimizes \(\sum_j D_\phi(c, S_j)\) and is \((\phi')^{-1}\{J^{-1}\sum_j \phi'(S_j)\}\); the second-argument centroid minimizes \(\sum_j D_\phi(S_j, c)\) and is the mean reliability for every \(\phi\) (Lee, 2026, Table 2 and Appendix B):

potential\(\phi(x)\)first-argument centroid
"squared"\(x^2/2\)mean reliability
"kl"\(x\log x + (1-x)\log(1-x)\)informativeness \(I\)
"burg"\(-\log x\)harmonic mean

The dispersion is the minimum average divergence. On the first side of "kl" it is the dispersion \(H\) of kl_dispersion(); on the second side it is the mean Bernoulli divergence of the reliabilities from their mean. The two need not agree: for the reliabilities 0.2 and 0.8 both centroids are 0.5, but the dispersions are \(\log(5/4) \approx 0.2231\) and about 0.1927. For "burg" the dispersions are the logarithm of the ratio of the geometric to the harmonic mean (first side) and of the arithmetic to the geometric mean (second side); for "squared" both are half the variance of the reliabilities, with divisor \(J\).

References

Lee, J. (2026). The geometry of informativeness: A Bregman-centroid diagnostic for partial pooling in multisite trials. Unpublished manuscript.

Examples

S <- c(0.2, 0.8)
bregman_centroid(S, "kl")
#> [1] 0.5
bregman_dispersion(S, "kl", side = "first")
#> [1] 0.2231436
bregman_dispersion(S, "kl", side = "second")
#> [1] 0.1927448

S <- site_reliability(se = c(0.10, 0.15, 0.20, 0.30), sigma_tau = 0.2)
sapply(c("squared", "kl", "burg"), function(p) bregman_centroid(S, p))
#>   squared        kl      burg 
#> 0.5619231 0.5714286 0.4961240
